evidence.quote: N-Methylmorpholine (10 mL, 91 mmol; purchased from Chemcraft, 99%) was dissolved in acetonitrile.
The reaction mixture was stirred for one hour at room temperature.
The resulting precipitate of lead (II) bromide (PbBr₂) was removed by filtration and washed thoroughly with water.
The resulting solid was dissolved in an ethanol, and any residual PbBr₂ was removed by filtration.

Ionic conductivity was characterized by impedance spectroscopy using an HP 4284A precision LCR meter (Hewlett-Packard, Japan). For the measurements, the OIPC sample was pressed by uniaxial compression at a pressure of 30 MPa, and silver powder electrodes were pressed onto the ends of the pellet also at 30 MPa. The measurements were performed using a two-electrode configuration in step-isotherm mode under the following conditions: low vacuum (residual pressure: 50 mTorr), a signal amplitude of 30 mV, and a frequency range of 3∙10¹ to 1∙10⁶ Hz.
For the measurements, the OIPC sample was pressed by uniaxial compression at a pressure of 30 MPa, and silver powder electrodes were pressed onto the ends of the pellet also at 30 MPa.
